target_customer: Dental practices and clinics that handle patient insurance in-house
problem: Clinics spend well over 100 hours a month on insurance verification, claims, billing and payer calls.
business_model: B2B SaaS and service subscription, with human-in-the-loop support; a directory lists pricing from $49 per month, unverified
product_category: Dental revenue cycle automation (voice and workflow AI agents)

founders.name: Johnny Chen
previous_startups: AI B2B cold email startup backed by SoftBank, reached $1M ARR

founders.name: Matt Kerrigan
prior_employers: a startup acquired by Nordstrom (ML role)
previous_startups: Salezilla (LLM cold email tool, still operating)

founders.name: Tejas Konduru
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the role.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents that call payers plus practice management integrations and claims workflows are standard AI engineering with messy integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Writing into practice management systems gives some lock-in, but several voice AI vendors target payer calls and the models are widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy of Toothy was found; vendor names come from undated 2026 comparison pages and are not confirmed as of founding.

market_need_then: The company says the average clinic spends 160+ hours monthly on insurance tasks; its site cites anonymous outcomes such as collection ratio from 50.8 to 97.2 percent, self-reported.

branding.domain_note: Uses toothy.ai, a descriptive name on an .ai domain.

identity.visual_style: Purple primary brand color chosen for its link to AI and healthcare, per an agency case study.

brand_strength.rationale: A playful, memorable dental name with a professionally redesigned site during YC; no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Toothy AI is active with about 15 people after Winter 2025. Second-time founders in AI outbound sales moved into dental insurance and reportedly closed a seed in March 2025 with Pioneer Fund. A job post says the company grew 30x during the batch, which is self-reported. No exit or failure signals were found, so the outcome remains early stage.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: Caplight and Startups.fm say $500K total, Yespress about $130K, Preqin undisclosed, so no amount is recorded. A $35M raise story for a company called Lassie appeared in results and was not attributed to Toothy. Competitor search returned undated or 2026 vendor blogs, so the dated list is empty. Name origin not stated. Founder education not found.
